annotations.description: The player mulliganed a 7-card hand that was very keepable. The hand had 5 lands (4 Forest + Thriving Grove), a 3-drop (Shambling Suit) and a 4-drop (Drownyard Explorers). While the hand is land-heavy, it curves out reasonably with a turn 3 Shambling Suit and turn 4 Drownyard Explorers (which creates a Clue to boost Shambling Suit). In Limited, a hand with lands and playable spells on curve should generally be kept. Mulliganing to 6 loses a card for no good reason — this hand isn't close to unplayable.
annotations.actionTaken: Mulliganed to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has sufficient mana, a reasonable curve with turn 3 and turn 4 plays, and synergy between Shambling Suit and the Clue from Drownyard Explorers.

annotations.description: Keeping a 6-card hand with 4 Forests and 2 spells (Might of the Masses, Roar of Challenge) that both require creatures to function. This hand has zero creatures and will do literally nothing until creatures are drawn. The player will spend early turns just playing lands and passing.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept a 6-card hand with no creatures and only creature-dependent spells
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 5 seeking a hand with at least one creature. A 5-card hand with a creature and lands would function much better than this hand which is effectively all blanks until a creature is drawn.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Aggressive Urge, a cantrip that replaces itself with a card draw, when there was mana available and no better use for the mana. With no combat tricks to hold up and no other instant-speed interaction in hand, casting the cantrip to dig deeper into the deck would have been strictly better.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Aggressive Urge
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Vedalken Engineer to draw a card and dig deeper into the deck, since there's no reason to hold the mana open with the current hand.

annotations.description: Cast Shambling Suit (which enters as a 1/3 since only itself is an artifact/enchantment on the battlefield) instead of Dutiful Replicator (a 3/2 body). With no other artifacts or enchantments in play, Shambling Suit is a much worse creature. Additionally, should play Thriving Grove before casting to ensure the land drop isn't missed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shambling Suit as a 1/3
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Grove first (enters tapped), then cast Dutiful Replicator (3/2) using Forest + Island + Thriving Isle. The 3/2 body is much more impactful than a 1/3, and Shambling Suit could be cast later when more artifacts/enchantments are in play to make it larger.

annotations.description: Passed with 2 available mana and no other plays, declining to cast Aggressive Urge (a cantrip that draws a card) on one of their creatures. Since there were no other uses for the mana this turn, casting the cantrip to dig deeper into the deck was strictly better than doing nothing. The +1/+1 combat trick value is minimal with no attackers available this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Aggressive Urge, wasting 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Dutiful Replicator (or Vedalken Engineer) to draw a card and potentially find useful spells for upcoming turns.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Aggressive Urge when the 2 available mana would otherwise go completely unused this turn. While there's no combat benefit (no attackers), the card draw from Aggressive Urge is valuable, and the mana is wasted anyway since Shambling Suit (3 mana) and Primordial Sage (6 mana) can't be cast with only 2 lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge, letting 2 mana go unused
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting any creature to draw a card, since the mana would be wasted otherwise and digging for lands/cards is important when behind on development

annotations.description: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge with exactly 2 mana available ({1}{G}) and no other plays. Aggressive Urge is a cantrip that replaces itself, and with expensive cards in hand (Primordial Sage at 6 mana), cycling through the deck to find lands or cheaper plays would have been valuable. The +1/+1 combat trick aspect has some value being held, but with the mana going to waste anyway, the card draw is more important.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 2 untapped mana unused
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Dutiful Replicator or Vedalken Engineer to draw a card and cycle through the deck while using the available mana

annotations.description: Declined to block Dutiful Replicator 3/2 with Rhonas the Indomitable 5/5 (indestructible, deathtouch). Rhonas cannot be destroyed and would kill the Replicator for free. Instead, Haiku Lucky took 3 unnecessary damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 3 damage from Dutiful Replicator.
annotations.betterLine: Block Dutiful Replicator with Rhonas the Indomitable to kill the 3/2 for free while taking no permanent damage due to indestructible.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge in precombat main phase when it would draw a card (cantrip) that could be a land drop needed to reach 6 mana for Primordial Sage/Warden of the Woods. The opponent's creatures are tapped/sick so there's no combat trick value to save it for. With 1 land drop remaining, drawing before combat and potentially playing a land is strictly better.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Aggressive Urge
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge on any creature (e.g., Dutiful Replicator or Shambling Suit) to draw a card, potentially play a land to get closer to 6 mana, then proceed to combat.

annotations.description: Opponent has zero available blockers — Rhonas can't block (no other creature with power 4+) and Primeval Herald has summoning sickness. All three creatures could attack unblocked for 6 damage (or 7 with Aggressive Urge). Passing up this much free damage is a huge mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Dutiful Replicator, Shambling Suit, Vedalken Engineer) for 6 unblocked damage, potentially casting Aggressive Urge on one attacker for 7 damage and a card draw.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge during combat when the opponent had no meaningful blockers available (Rhonas can't block without a 4+ power creature, Primeval Herald is sick). Aggressive Urge is a cantrip (+1/+1 and draw a card) that would have dealt 1 extra damage and drawn a card, and the player couldn't use their mana for their 6-drops (Primordial Sage/Warden) this turn anyway since they only have 5 regular lands plus artifact-restricted Vedalken Engineer mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge on an unblocked attacker (like Dutiful Replicator or Shambling Suit) to deal 1 extra damage and draw a card, since the mana couldn't be spent on anything more impactful this turn.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge in postcombat main phase with a land drop still remaining. Aggressive Urge is a cantrip that draws a card, and with the land drop unused, casting it now could find a 6th land to play immediately, enabling Primordial Sage or Warden of the Woods next turn. The combat trick value of +1/+1 is minimal given the opponent's Rhonas has deathtouch/indestructible.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Aggressive Urge, ending the turn with an unused land drop and 2 mana available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting any creature to draw a card, then potentially play a land if drawn, getting closer to casting the 6-mana threats in hand (Primordial Sage or Warden of the Woods).

annotations.description: Shambling Suit (2/3) is being used to block when Vedalken Engineer (1/1) could block Primeval Herald (3/1) and kill it just as effectively (1 damage kills a 1-toughness creature). Using the more valuable Shambling Suit as a blocker wastes a better body when a disposable 1/1 would accomplish the same thing.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with Shambling Suit, losing a 2/3 body
annotations.betterLine: Block Primeval Herald with Vedalken Engineer (1/1 kills the 3/1 Herald equally well) and preserve Shambling Suit. Take 5 from Rhonas either way since it's indestructible.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Aggressive Urge during combat when Shambling Suit (2/3) was blocking Primeval Herald (3/1). Without the pump, both creatures trade and die. With Aggressive Urge, Shambling Suit becomes 3/4, survives combat at 3/1, and Gem3F Philo draws a card. This is pure upside - saves a creature and cantrips.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Shambling Suit to trade with Primeval Herald.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Shambling Suit to make it 3/4, allowing it to survive the 3 damage from Primeval Herald while still killing it, plus drawing a card.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Aggressive Urge as a cantrip during opponent's combat phase. The mana spent (2 mana from untapped lands) would go unused otherwise since all lands untap for their next turn. Aggressive Urge replaces itself (draws a card) and gives +1/+1 to a creature, making it essentially free value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Aggressive Urge
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Dutiful Replicator (or Vedalken Engineer) to draw a card for free, since the 2 mana would otherwise go unused before untapping next turn.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures that can block (Rhonas is tapped, Spectral Hunt-Caller has summoning sickness) and all opponent's lands are tapped, so no combat tricks possible. Dutiful Replicator could attack for 3 free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Dutiful Replicator for 3 unblockable damage, bringing opponent from 17 to 14.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Aggressive Urge during combat on what appears to be an unblocked Dutiful Replicator. Aggressive Urge would deal 1 extra damage (bringing opponent to 13 instead of 14) and draw a card, which is pure upside. The 2 mana cost doesn't prevent casting either 6-drop next turn since they'll have 7+ mana sources available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without casting Aggressive Urge
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting the attacking Dutiful Replicator to deal 1 extra damage and draw a card for free value

annotations.description: At 6 life facing 9 damage from Rhonas (5/5) and Spectral Hunt-Caller (4/4), Gem3F Philo passed without casting Aggressive Urge on their only blocker (Dutiful Replicator). Aggressive Urge is a cantrip that draws a card and buffs the blocker - crucial when behind and desperate for answers. The 2 mana saved doesn't enable any other meaningful play this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge on Dutiful Replicator to make it 4/3 and draw a card, potentially finding an answer to survive the following turn.

annotations.description: At 6 life facing lethal on board next turn (Rhonas 5/5 + Spectral Hunt-Caller 4/4 + Elderleaf Mentor 3/2 + Elf token = 13+ power), player passed postcombat main without casting Aggressive Urge, a cantrip that costs only 2 mana and could find a crucial answer like Band Together or Roar of Challenge.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase without casting any spells, ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aggressive Urge targeting Dutiful Replicator (or any creature) to draw a card and potentially find an answer to the lethal board state. The 2-mana cantrip is essentially free value and critical when behind and at low life.

annotations.description: Missed lethal. With opponent at 6 life and only Dutiful Replicator 3/2 and Vedalken Engineer 1/1 as available blockers (Warden of the Woods is summoning sick), casting Roar of Challenge on Rhonas the Indomitable would force all blockers onto Rhonas (who gains indestructible via Ferocious), leaving Spectral Hunt-Caller 4/4, Elderleaf Mentor 3/2, and Elf Warrior 1/1 completely unblocked for 8 damage — lethal against 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase without casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Roar of Challenge targeting Rhonas the Indomitable (forcing all blockers onto indestructible Rhonas), then attack with all creatures for 8 unblocked damage, winning the game.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with only 2 available blockers (Warden is summoning sick). Attacking with all 4 creatures forces opponent to leave at least 2 unblocked. With Might of the Masses in hand (+4/+4 for 4 creatures), any unblocked creature deals lethal. Even without the pump spell, all-out attack deals at minimum 4 damage (opponent to 2).
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Rhonas and Spectral Hunt-Caller, leaving Elderleaf Mentor and Elf token back.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all four creatures. Opponent must block Rhonas (or die). With only one remaining blocker, at least two creatures get through. Cast Might of the Masses on an unblocked creature for guaranteed lethal damage.

annotations.description: Blocked Rhonas the Indomitable (5/5 deathtouch, indestructible) with Warden of the Woods (5/7), losing the best creature on the board for nothing since Rhonas is indestructible. Meanwhile, blocking Spectral Hunt-Caller with the 1/1 Vedalken Engineer wastes the opportunity to kill Hunt-Caller with Warden.
annotations.actionTaken: Warden of the Woods blocked Rhonas (dies to deathtouch, Rhonas survives due to indestructible), Vedalken Engineer blocked Spectral Hunt-Caller (Engineer dies, Hunt-Caller survives).
annotations.betterLine: Block Rhonas with Vedalken Engineer (1/1 dies to deathtouch, no trample so 0 damage through) or Dutiful Replicator, and block Spectral Hunt-Caller with Warden of the Woods (Warden survives at 5/3, Hunt-Caller dies). This saves the Warden, kills Hunt-Caller, and only loses a 1/1.

annotations.description: Haiku Lucky targeted Spectral Hunt-Caller with Might of the Masses instead of the unblocked Rhonas the Indomitable. Rhonas is attacking unblocked, and with +5/+5 from Might of the Masses (5 creatures), Rhonas would deal 10 damage to the opponent at 6 life — lethal. Instead, targeting the blocked Hunt-Caller (which doesn't have trample) wastes the pump spell's damage on the 1/1 blocker, and Rhonas only deals 5, leaving the opponent at 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Spectral Hunt-Caller (blocked by Vedalken Engineer 1/1) with Might of the Masses
annotations.betterLine: Target Rhonas the Indomitable (unblocked) with Might of the Masses for 10 unblocked damage against an opponent at 6 life — lethal.

annotations.description: Spectral Hunt-Caller (10/8) is blocked by a 1/1 Vedalken Engineer. If it doesn't already have trample, all its damage is absorbed by the blocker and only 5 damage from Rhonas gets through (opponent goes to 1 HP instead of dying). The player had exactly {2}{G} available to activate Rhonas targeting Spectral Hunt-Caller, granting it +2/+0 and trample, which would deal 11 trample damage through the 1/1 blocker — combined with Rhonas's 5 unblocked damage, that's 16 total against 6 HP, guaranteed lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating Rhonas's ability, potentially missing lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Rhonas the Indomitable ({2}{G}) targeting Spectral Hunt-Caller to give it +2/+0 and trample, ensuring all excess combat damage tramples through the 1/1 blocker for lethal.
